pr.title: feat(cake_gdn): opt-in exact sequence split for the Cake GDN prefill on SM103
pr.body:
The Cake GDN (Gated DeltaNet) chunked prefill in FlashInfer (`chunk_gated_delta_rule(..., backend="cake_gdn")`) has two routes: an unsplit (non-CP) route and a context-parallel route (`use_cp`). Both use BF16 q/k/v with FP32 state. This PR adds a third route that is opt-in: `use_affine_split=True`. It is keyword-only and defaults to `False`, so existing behavior is unchanged. The route is an exact sequence split. Each sequence is divided into chunk-aligned segments. Pass 1 runs the existing prefill on each segment along with an identity-column chain, which yields per-token coefficients and each segment's transfer and offset. Pass 2 composes the incoming state across segments and corrects the outputs. The math is exact. The route is SM103 only and takes one sequence per call (N=1). Sequences of 1024 tokens or fewer run the unsplit kernel.

NVIDIA GB300 (SM103, sm_103a), CUDA 13.4 (nvcc 13.4.92), driver 580.159.03, torch 2.14.1+cu130. CUDA graph, cold L2, median of 5 alternating groups × 50 replays. N=1, BF16 q/k/v, FP32 gates/state, initial state present, final state written. Latency is in µs. Shape is (num q heads, num v heads) with head dim 128. P is the number of segments, and P=1 means the unsplit kernel runs. Each ratio is baseline latency divided by split latency, so a value above 1 means the split is faster. A **bold** ratio means the split is slower than that baseline.

+"""Opt-in exact sequence split of the Cake GDN prefill on SM103.
+
+``chunk_gated_delta_rule(..., backend="cake_gdn", use_affine_split=True)``
+cuts a sequence of ``L`` tokens into ``P`` chunk-aligned segments and runs
+them in one wave instead of one walk:
+
+* pass 1 (``PASS1``) walks segment 0 from the initial state into the output
+  and, for every later segment ``s``, walks it once from zeros (its local
+  output ``o_loc`` and state ``B_s``) and once from the identity with
+  ``v = 0`` (its transfer ``c`` and ``M_s``);
+* pass 2 (``PASS2_W*``) composes the carried states
+  ``h_in(s + 1) = h_in(s) M_s + B_s`` and corrects every later segment's
+  output, ``O = o_loc + h_in(s) c``, rounded to BF16 once, and writes the
+  final state.
+
+The result is the same recurrence in another summation order: it is not
+bitwise equal to the unsplit route when ``P > 1``.
+
+Segment rule (both kernels read the live ``cu_seqlens``): with ``start =
+clamp(cu[n], 0, T)``, ``L = clamp(cu[n + 1], start, T) - start`` and
+``nchunks = ceil(L / 64)``, ``P = 1`` when ``L == 0`` and
+``clamp(nchunks // c_min, 1, p_cap)`` otherwise; segment ``s`` holds the
+tokens ``[start + 64 * floor(s * nchunks / P), start + min(64 * floor((s +
+1) * nchunks / P), L))``.  ``p_cap`` and ``c_min`` are plan constants of the
+device and the value-head count only (:func:`plan_constants`), so a
+sequence's bits do not depend on the other sequences of a batch.
+
+A plan entry owns its workspaces, allocated and zeroed once: the launch path
+allocates nothing, reads nothing back from the device and issues no memset
+(pass 2 leaves its flags and ticket at zero after every launch), so a warm
+entry is CUDA-graph capturable.  Eager entries live in a bounded LRU keyed by
+the geometry and the stream; a capture moves the warm entry of its key and
+stream out of the LRU into a pinned list, so the captured graph keeps its
+workspaces for the life of the process and eager calls never share them.
+Replays of one graph must not overlap each other.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import collections
+import functools
+from typing import Any, NamedTuple, Optional
+
+import torch
+import tvm_ffi
+
+from ...jit import cake_gdn_affine_split as _programs
+
+__all__ = [
+    "C_MIN",
+    "P_MAX",
+    "SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS",
+    "SplitPlan",
+    "chunk_gated_delta_rule_gdn_affine_split_sm100",
+    "clear_affine_split_plans",
+    "pass1_grid",
+    "pass2_grid",
+    "plan_constants",
+    "plan_split",
+    "segment_count",
+    "tile_cap",
+]
+
+_TARGET = "sm_103a"
+_HEAD_SIZE = 128
+_CHUNK = 64
+#: Bytes of the pass-1 device tensor-map scratch per CTA.
+_TMAP_BYTES = 512
+#: The largest segment count per value-head count on SM103 (one pass-1 wave).
+P_MAX: dict[int, int] = {4: 8, 8: 5, 16: 2, 32: 1}
+#: The fewest chunks per segment per value-head count.
+C_MIN: dict[int, int] = {4: 8, 8: 8, 16: 16, 32: 16}
+#: A call whose longest possible sequence has at most this many tokens runs
+#: the unsplit kernel: on SM103 two segments do not beat it there.
+SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS = 1024
+#: The pass-2 program name of each value-head count (its compose slice width).
+_PASS2_NAMES: dict[int, str] = {
+    4: "PASS2_W4",
+    8: "PASS2_W8",
+    16: "PASS2_W16",
+    32: "PASS2_W16",
+}
+_SLICE_WIDTH: dict[int, int] = {4: 4, 8: 8, 16: 16, 32: 16}
+_EAGER_LIMIT = 8
+
+_PASS1_ARGS = (
+    "Q",
+    "K",
+    "V",
+    "O",
+    "gate",
+    "beta",
+    "cu_seqlens",
+    "state_indices",
+    "initial_state",
+    "output_state",
+    "checkpoint_state",
+    "cu_checkpoints",
+    "tensormap_workspace",
+    "initial_state_stride_slot",
+    "output_state_stride_slot",
+    "checkpoint_every_n_tokens",
+    "scale",
+    "num_seqs",
+    "total_tokens",
+    "num_q_heads",
+    "num_v_heads",
+    "total_tiles",
+    "o_loc",
+    "c",
+    "bm",
+    "p_cap",
+    "c_min",
+    "grid_x",
+    "grid_y",
+    "grid_z",
+)
+_PASS2_ARGS = (
+    "o_loc",
+    "c_rows",
+    "c_tma",
+    "bm",
+    "hpub",
+    "hpub_tma",
+    "output",
+    "output_state",
+    "flags",
+    "ticket",
+    "cu_seqlens",
+    "output_state_stride_slot",
+    "total_tokens",
+    "num_seqs",
+    "num_heads",
+    "p_cap",
+    "c_min",
+    "grid_x",
+    "grid_y",
+    "grid_z",
+)
+
+
+def tile_cap(num_heads: int, sm_count: int) -> int:
+    """The largest segment count whose pass-1 tiles fit one wave:
+    ``num_heads * (4 * P - 2) <= sm_count``, at least 1."""
+
+    return max(1, (sm_count // num_heads + 2) // 4)
+
+
+def plan_constants(
+    num_heads: int, sm_count: int, split_count: Optional[int] = None
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """``(p_cap, c_min)``: the planner's constants, or with ``split_count``
+    the forced cap ``min(split_count, tile_cap)`` at one chunk per segment."""
+
+    cap = tile_cap(num_heads, sm_count)
+    if split_count is not None:
+        return min(int(split_count), cap), 1
+    return min(cap, P_MAX[num_heads]), C_MIN[num_heads]
+
+
+def segment_count(length: int, p_cap: int, c_min: int) -> int:
+    """The segment count of a sequence of ``length`` tokens."""
+
+    if length <= 0:
+        return 1
+    return max(1, min(p_cap, -(-length // _CHUNK) // c_min))
+
+
+class SplitPlan(NamedTuple):
+    p_cap: int
+    c_min: int
+    #: The segment count of the longest possible sequence: 1 means every
+    #: sequence of the call runs unsplit.
+    p_bound: int
+
+
+def plan_split(
+    *,
+    num_heads: int,
+    max_seqlen: int,
+    sm_count: int,
+    split_count: Optional[int] = None,
+) -> SplitPlan:
+    """The plan constants and the host bound on the segment count.
+
+    Without ``split_count``, ``max_seqlen <= SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS`` gives
+    ``p_bound = 1``. A larger bound keeps the device segment rule for every
+    live length, so a shorter live sequence of that call may still split."""
+
+    p_cap, c_min = plan_constants(num_heads, sm_count, split_count)
+    if split_count is None and max_seqlen <= SPLIT_MIN_TOKENS:
+        return SplitPlan(p_cap, c_min, 1)
+    return SplitPlan(p_cap, c_min, segment_count(max_seqlen, p_cap, c_min))
+
+
+def pass1_grid(
+    num_seqs: int, num_heads: int, p_cap: int, sm_count: int
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """``(total_tiles, grid_x)`` of pass 1: segment 0 has ``2 * H`` tiles,
+    every later segment ``4 * H``; one wave of at most ``sm_count`` CTAs."""
+
+    tiles = num_seqs * num_heads * (4 * p_cap - 2)
+    return tiles, min(tiles, sm_count)
+
+
+def pass2_grid(
+    num_seqs: int,
+    num_heads: int,
+    total_tokens: int,
+    p_cap: int,
+    slice_width: int,
+    sm_count: int,
+) -> int:
+    """Pass 2's grid: every compose ticket, then correction CTAs up to two
+    CTAs per SM (at least 32), never more than the work bound."""
+
+    compose = num_seqs * num_heads * _HEAD_SIZE // slice_width
+    bound = compose + 2 * num_heads * (-(-total_tokens // 128) + num_seqs * p_cap)
+    return min(bound, compose + max(2 * sm_count - compose, 32))
+
+
+def _pass2_program(num_heads: int) -> Any:
+    """The pass-2 program of a value-head count."""
+
+    return getattr(_programs, _PASS2_NAMES[num_heads])
+
+
+def _check_args(program: Any, expected: tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
+    if tuple(program.args) != expected:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"the generated {program.name} binding takes {list(program.args)}; "
+            f"the host spells {list(expected)}"
+        )
+
+
+@functools.cache
+def _entries(device_index: int, pass2: Any) -> tuple[Any, Optional[Any]]:
+    """The loaded pass-1 and pass-2 entries of one device (``pass2`` None:
+    pass 1 alone)."""
+
+    _check_args(_programs.PASS1, _PASS1_ARGS)
+    capability = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device_index)
+    target = _programs.PASS1.target_for(capability)
+    if target != _TARGET:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"the Cake GDN affine-split programs ship no build for compute "
+            f"capability {capability[0]}.{capability[1]}"
+        )
+    first = _programs.PASS1.entry(target)
+    if pass2 is None:
+        return first, None
+    _check_args(pass2, _PASS2_ARGS)
+    return first, pass2.entry(target)
+
+
+class _Entry:
+    """One plan entry: launch constants and the workspaces it owns."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        device: torch.device,
+        sm_count: int,
+        num_seqs: int,
+        total_tokens: int,
+        num_q_heads: int,
+        num_heads: int,
+        p_cap: int,
+        c_min: int,
+        has_initial_state: bool,
+        output_final_state: bool,
+        gates_present: tuple[bool, bool],
+        cu_int64: bool,
+    ) -> None:
+        n, t, h = num_seqs, total_tokens, num_heads
+        self.num_seqs, self.total_tokens = n, t
+        self.num_q_heads, self.num_heads = num_q_heads, h
+        self.p_cap, self.c_min = p_cap, c_min
+        self.tiles1, self.grid1 = pass1_grid(n, h, p_cap, sm_count)
+        self.run_pass2 = p_cap >= 2
+        pass2 = _pass2_program(h) if self.run_pass2 else None
+        self.grid2 = (
+            pass2_grid(n, h, t, p_cap, _SLICE_WIDTH[h], sm_count)
+            if self.run_pass2
+            else 0
+        )
+        self.pass1, self.pass2 = _entries(int(device.index), pass2)
+        f32, bf16, i32 = torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.int32
+        d = _HEAD_SIZE
+        self.o_loc = torch.zeros(t, h, d, dtype=f32, device=device)
+        self.c = torch.zeros(t, h, d, dtype=bf16, device=device)
+        self.bm = torch.zeros(n, 2, p_cap, h, d, d, dtype=f32, device=device)
+        self.hpub = torch.zeros(
+            n * max(p_cap - 1, 1) * h * 2, d, d, dtype=bf16, device=device
+        )
+        self.flags = torch.zeros(n, p_cap, h, 2, dtype=torch.uint32, device=device)
+        self.ticket = torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.uint32, device=device)
+        self.tensormap_workspace = torch.zeros(
+            self.grid1 * _TMAP_BYTES, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+        )
+        self.empty_i32 = torch.zeros(1, dtype=i32, device=device)
+        self.empty_state = torch.zeros(1, dtype=f32, device=device)
+        self.zero_state = (
+            None
+            if has_initial_state
+            else torch.zeros(n, h, d, d, dtype=f32, device=device)
+        )
+        self.scratch_state = (
+            None
+            if output_final_state
+            else torch.empty(n, h, d, d, dtype=f32, device=device)
+        )
+        self.unit_gates = (
+            None if all(gates_present) else torch.ones(t, h, dtype=f32, device=device)
+        )
+        self.cu32 = torch.zeros(n + 1, dtype=i32, device=device) if cu_int64 else None
+        self.warm = False
+
+    def launch(
+        self,
+        *,
+        q: torch.Tensor,
+        k: torch.Tensor,
+        v: torch.Tensor,
+        g: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+        beta: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+        scale: float,
+        cu_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+        initial_state: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+        output: torch.Tensor,
+        output_state: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+    ) -> None:
+        cu = cu_seqlens
+        if self.cu32 is not None:
+            self.cu32.copy_(cu_seqlens)
+            cu = self.cu32
+        h0 = initial_state if initial_state is not None else self.zero_state

+from flashinfer.gdn_prefill import chunk_gated_delta_rule

+D = 128
+SCALE = 1.0 / math.sqrt(D)
+HEADS = [(2, 4), (4, 8), (8, 16), (16, 32)]
+GATE = {"real": 1.10, "stress": 1.20}

+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def _require_sm103():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+        pytest.skip("requires CUDA")
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (10, 3):
+        pytest.skip("the Cake GDN affine-split route ships for SM103 only")
+    if prefill_mod._chunk_gated_delta_rule_gdn_affine_split_sm100 is None:
+        pytest.skip("the Cake GDN affine-split backend is not installed")

+def _split_module():
+    from flashinfer.gdn_kernels.blackwell import cake_gdn_affine_split

+    return cake_gdn_affine_split

+def _sm_count() -> int:
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).multi_processor_count

+def _problem(hq, hv, t, kind="real", seed=0):
+    """Q/K L2-normalized; ``real``: Mamba-style decays, ``stress``: decays in
+    [0.999, 1] with beta near 1 and a unit-scale initial state."""
+
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(
+        1234
+        + 1000003 * seed
+        + 7919 * hq
+        + 104729 * hv
+        + t
+        + (17 if kind == "stress" else 0)
+    )
+
+    def rn(*shape):
+        return torch.randn(*shape, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32, generator=gen)
+
+    q = torch.nn.functional.normalize(rn(t, hq, D), dim=-1).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    k = torch.nn.functional.normalize(rn(t, hq, D), dim=-1).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    v = rn(t, hv, D).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    if kind == "real":
+        a = torch.empty(hv, device="cuda").uniform_(1.0, 16.0, generator=gen)
+        dt = torch.exp(
+            torch.empty(hv, device="cuda").uniform_(
+                math.log(1e-3), math.log(1e-1), generator=gen
+            )
+        )
+        dt_bias = dt + torch.log(-torch.expm1(-dt))
+        g = torch.exp(-a * torch.nn.functional.softplus(rn(t, hv) + dt_bias))
+        beta = torch.sigmoid(rn(t, hv))
+        h0 = 0.05 * rn(1, hv, D, D)
+    else:
+        g = 1.0 - 0.001 * torch.rand(t, hv, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+        beta = (0.9 + 0.1 * torch.rand(t, hv, device="cuda", generator=gen)).clamp_(
+            max=0.99999
+        )
+        h0 = rn(1, hv, D, D)
+    return dict(
+        q=q.contiguous(),
+        k=k.contiguous(),
+        v=v.contiguous(),
+        g=g.contiguous(),
+        beta=beta.contiguous(),
+        h0=h0.contiguous(),
+        hq=hq,
+        hv=hv,
+        t=t,
+    )
+
+
+def _fp64_reference(pr, start=0, end=None):
+    """Per-token FP64 recurrence over the tokens [start, end); state [H, V, K]."""
+
+    end = pr["t"] if end is None else end
+    hv, hq = pr["hv"], pr["hq"]
+    rep = hv // hq
+    q = pr["q"][start:end].double().repeat_interleave(rep, dim=1)
+    k = pr["k"][start:end].double().repeat_interleave(rep, dim=1)
+    v = pr["v"][start:end].double()
+    g = pr["g"][start:end].double()
+    beta = pr["beta"][start:end].double()
+    state = pr["h0"][0].double().transpose(-1, -2).contiguous()  # [H, K, V]
+    out = torch.empty(end - start, hv, D, dtype=torch.float64, device="cuda")
+    for i in range(end - start):
+        state = g[i].view(-1, 1, 1) * state
+        old_v = torch.einsum("hk,hkv->hv", k[i], state)
+        delta = beta[i].view(-1, 1) * (v[i] - old_v)
+        state = state + k[i].unsqueeze(-1) * delta.unsqueeze(-2)
+        out[i] = SCALE * torch.einsum("hk,hkv->hv", q[i], state)
+    return out, state.transpose(-1, -2).unsqueeze(0)
+
+
+def _call(pr, *, cu=None, output=None, output_state=None, **kwargs):
+    t, hv = pr["t"], pr["hv"]
+    if cu is None:
+        cu = torch.tensor([0, t], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    if output is None:
+        output = torch.empty(t, hv, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    if output_state is None:
+        output_state = torch.empty(1, hv, D, D, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    kwargs.setdefault("initial_state", pr["h0"])
+    return chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+        pr["q"],
+        pr["k"],
+        pr["v"],
+        g=pr["g"],
+        beta=pr["beta"],
+        scale=SCALE,
+        output_final_state=True,
+        cu_seqlens=cu,
+        output=output,
+        output_state=output_state,
+        backend="cake_gdn",
+        **kwargs,
+    )
+
+
+def _rel_rms(x, ref):
+    x, ref = x.double(), ref.double()
+    return float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(x - ref) / torch.linalg.vector_norm(ref))
+
+
+def _p_bound(hv, t, split_count=None):
+    return (
+        _split_module()
+        .plan_split(
+            num_heads=hv, max_seqlen=t, sm_count=_sm_count(), split_count=split_count
+        )
+        .p_bound
+    )
+
+
+def _zero_words():
+    split = _split_module()
+    entries = list(split._EAGER.values()) + list(split._PINNED.values())
+    return all(
+        int(e.flags.count_nonzero()) == 0 and int(e.ticket.count_nonzero()) == 0
+        for e in entries
+    )

+    pr = _problem(hq, hv, t, kind)
+    ref_o, ref_s = _fp64_reference(pr)
+    o_split, s_split = _call(pr, use_affine_split=True)
+    o_base, s_base = _call(pr, use_cp=False)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    for name, x, base, ref in (
+        ("output", o_split, o_base, ref_o),
+        ("state", s_split, s_base, ref_s),
+    ):
+        assert torch.isfinite(x).all(), name
+        err, err_base = _rel_rms(x, ref), _rel_rms(base, ref)
+        assert err <= GATE[kind] * err_base, (name, err, err_base)
+        assert err < 1e-2, (name, err)
+    return pr, o_split, s_split, o_base, s_base

+            _call(layers[0], cu=cu, use_affine_split=True)  # warm a fresh entry
+        stream.synchronize()
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            run_layers()
+        graphs.append(graph)
+        assert len(split._PINNED) == len(graphs) and not split._EAGER
+    for graph in graphs:
+        for o, st in zip(outs, states, strict=True):
+            o.fill_(float("nan"))
+            st.fill_(float("nan"))
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert _zero_words()
+        for pr, o, st in zip(layers, outs, states, strict=True):
+            o_eager, s_eager = _call(pr, use_affine_split=True)
+            assert torch.equal(o.view(torch.int16), o_eager.view(torch.int16))
+            assert torch.equal(st.view(torch.int32), s_eager.view(torch.int32))
+    split.clear_affine_split_plans()
+
+
+# --- rejections on the device -------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _unaligned_state():
+    return torch.zeros(8 * D * D + 1, device="cuda")[1:].view(1, 8, D, D)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "change,reason",
+    [
+        (dict(heads=6), "requires Hv in (4, 8, 16, 32), Hk == Hq and Hv % Hq == 0"),
+        (dict(cu=[0, 1000, 2048]), "supports one sequence (num_seqs == 1)"),
+        (
+            dict(cu=[0, 7, 2048, 9], cu_step=2),
+            "requires contiguous int32 or int64 cu_seqlens",
+        ),
+        (dict(h0="bf16"), "requires FP32 states with contiguous [H, V, K] rows"),
+        (
+            dict(h0="unaligned"),
+            "requires 16-byte aligned state pointers and slot strides",
+        ),
+        (dict(g="strided"), "requires contiguous FP32 g/beta [tokens, heads]"),
+        (
+            dict(q="f16"),
+            "requires contiguous BF16 q/k/v/output of head size 128 on one device",
+        ),
+    ],
+)
+def test_out_of_scope_calls_raise_before_any_launch(change, reason):
+    import re
+
+    hv = change.get("heads", 8)
+    pr = _problem(4, 8, 2048, "real")
+    q, k = pr["q"], pr["k"]
+    v = (
+        pr["v"]
+        if hv == 8
+        else torch.randn(2048, hv, D, device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)
+    )
+    g, beta = (
+        pr["g"][:, :1].expand(2048, hv).contiguous(),
+        pr["beta"][:, :1].expand(2048, hv).contiguous(),
+    )
+    h0 = torch.zeros(1, hv, D, D, device="cuda")
+    if change.get("h0") == "bf16":
+        h0 = h0.to(torch.bfloat16)
+    elif change.get("h0") == "unaligned":
+        h0 = _unaligned_state()
+    if change.get("g") == "strided":
+        g = torch.zeros(hv, 2048, device="cuda").t()
+    if change.get("q") == "f16":
+        q, k, v = q.half(), k.half(), v.half()
+    cu = torch.tensor(change.get("cu", [0, 2048]), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    cu = cu[:: change.get("cu_step", 1)]
+    output = torch.full(
+        (2048, max(4, hv), D), float("nan"), dtype=q.dtype, device="cuda"
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=re.escape(f"use_affine_split=True: {reason}")):
+        chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+            q,
+            k,
+            v,
+            g=g,
+            beta=beta,
+            scale=SCALE,
+            initial_state=h0,
+            output_final_state=True,
+            cu_seqlens=cu,
+            output=output,
+            backend="cake_gdn",
+            use_affine_split=True,
+        )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.isnan(output).all()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "cu_cpu,match",
+    [
+        ([0, 1], "spanning all input tokens"),
+        ([0, 2048, 4096], "cu_seqlens_cpu must have num_seqs \\+ 1 = 2 entries"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_host_offsets_are_checked_on_the_split_route(cu_cpu, match):
+    pr = _problem(4, 8, 4096, "real")
+    assert _p_bound(8, 4096) > 1
+    output = torch.full((4096, 8, D), float("nan"), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    with pytest.raises(NotImplementedError, match=match):
+        _call(pr, output=output, cu_seqlens_cpu=cu_cpu, use_affine_split=True)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    assert torch.isnan(output).all()
+    o_cpu, s_cpu = _call(pr, cu_seqlens_cpu=[0, 4096], use_affine_split=True)
+    o_cpu, s_cpu = o_cpu.clone(), s_cpu.clone()
+    o_dev, s_dev = _call(pr, use_affine_split=True)
+    assert torch.equal(o_cpu, o_dev) and torch.equal(s_cpu, s_dev)
+
+
+def test_scope_is_checked_before_the_gates_are_materialized():
+    """A log-domain gate is materialized by a launch; an out-of-scope state
+    must be rejected before it."""
+
+    pr = _problem(4, 8, 2048, "real")
+    log_g = torch.log(pr["g"].clamp_min(1e-30))
+    h0 = torch.zeros(1, 8, D, D, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+    def bad_call():
+        with pytest.raises(
+            ValueError,
+            match=r"use_affine_split=True: requires FP32 states with contiguous",
+        ):
+            chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+                pr["q"],
+                pr["k"],
+                pr["v"],
+                g=log_g,
+                beta=pr["beta"],
+                scale=SCALE,
+                initial_state=h0,
+                output_final_state=True,
+                cu_seqlens=torch.tensor([0, 2048], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+                backend="cake_gdn",
+                gate_domain="log",
+                use_affine_split=True,
+            )
+
+    assert _kernel_names(bad_call) == []
